summary: Close five review findings: record a coverage row when a release's report exists but no parser accepts its format, require a terminal report row before resume treats a release as done (consulting the scraped index for releases that list no report file at all), replace rather than upsert a rewritten release, re-apply the host allowlist on every redirect hop, and actually enforce MaxBodyBytes.
reason: All five were confirmed against the code during the publish review. (1) The report branch was gated on strings.EqualFold(f.Ext, "xlsx") while the annexure branch 48 lines above has no ext gate and dispatches on sniffed content; on a PDF-only report the whole block was skipped, ok stayed true, and no report-role coverage row was written at all, so the release was recorded complete while holding no weight vector, no weight totals and no quintile indices, and neither coverage nor verify could name the hole (verify degrades to skipped and exits 0). Measured off the committed index fixture the report-role split is 99 PDF-only, 48 xlsx and 1 with no report file across 148 weekly releases, so this silently affected the majority case. (2) loadCompleted keyed on the annexure row alone, so a release whose annexure committed and whose report then failed was skipped by every later ordinary sync and lost its report-derived rows permanently unless --refetch was used. (3) persistAnnexure and persistReport were upsert-only with no prior delete, so a rewritten release that dropped an item left the old item alive at the same as_of to be summed into a later basket or national average; the item basket is not constant upstream and revisions exists precisely because PBS rewrites releases. (4) checkOrigin ran once on the URL passed in, and the http.Client set no CheckRedirect, so Go's default followed up to 10 redirects without re-checking and an allowed PBS URL could bounce the fetch to loopback or a metadata address. The four existing origin tests all covered the initial URL only, so the gap was untested as well as unfixed. (5) MaxBodyBytes was declared and never referenced anywhere: the body was consumed with a bare io.ReadAll, so the documented 128 MiB cap did not exist. Its sibling protection in xlsx.go (a 64 MiB per-worksheet cap with an UncompressedSize64 pre-check) had landed correctly, so one half of that fix shipped and the other half was dead code. A first pass at (1) recorded upstream_404 when the index listed no report file at all, which was wrong: every CPI month lists no report-role file (measured from pbs_release_file — cpi-monthly carries annexure 48, construction 26, unknown 52 and zero report rows), so that fabricated a 'gone upstream' observation about a file that never existed. The corrected version records a row only when the file EXISTS but is unreadable, and uses covNotFetched rather than covUnparsed because nothing was fetched and no parse was attempted. loadCompleted consults pbs_release_file for the no-report-file case instead of requiring a placeholder row.
validated_outcome: go test -race ./... passes with zero failures. New regressions: TestLoadCompletedRequiresTerminalReport pins that only fetched/upstream_404/parse_failed report states count as terminal while transport_error and a missing report row stay retryable; TestDeleteReleaseRowsDropsStaleObservations pins that a rewrite clears the release and leaves neighbouring as_of rows intact; TestGetRefusesRedirectToDisallowedHost uses a non-resolvable target so a pass proves refusal happens before the request is issued; TestGetFollowsRedirectWithinAllowedHost keeps same-host redirects working; TestGetStopsAfterTooManyRedirects bounds a loop; TestGetRefusesOversizedBody and TestGetAcceptsBodyAtExactlyTheCap pin the cap and its off-by-one boundary. Policy refusals were also made non-retryable, which cut the pbsfetch package from 15.6s to 1.6s by removing pointless backoff on a decision that cannot change. Verified against a live panel on both series: spi-weekly records report rows not_fetched/not_fetched/not_fetched/fetched over a 4-release window with 10,404 price rows (2,601 each), 51 weight rows and null discipline 0/0; cpi-monthly writes ZERO report rows and zero fabricated upstream_404 rows. Index measurement from the same panel: spi-weekly report-role files are pdf 144 / xlsx 48, with exactly 1 weekly release listing no report file.
